gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_input survey reviewable alongside the already-landed helper.
The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status and queue bookkeeping, so the virtio_input lane can rely on that footing instead of reopening core-side work.
The live repo already has a bounded in-memory ring helper for queue shape and notification bookkeeping, which is the minimum queue-facing support the virtio_input starter depends on.

The first virtio_input-specific helper is already landed and now models identity snapshots, config bitmaps, ABS metadata, queue planning, ready-state gating, multitouch slot planning, and multitouch timestamp suppression without claiming transport parity.
Dedicated Phase 10 tests already keep the starter helper honest around capped string copies, queue planning, ready gating, reset behavior, and MSC_TIMESTAMP suppression.
The slice note already records what the landed helper covers so the survey can focus on the remaining roadmap gap rather than re-explaining the starter surface.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the current virtio_input roadmap gap explicit now that the repo already has a starter helper and test path.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that compares the live starter against the roadmap and prevents the repo from overstating input-driver progress.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory capability-setup helper that connects `virtinput_cfg_bits()`, `virtinput_cfg_abs()`, `input_set_capability()`, and `input_set_abs_params()` intent without claiming transport-backed config reads or input-core registration.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory multitouch slot-planning helper keyed off `ABS_MT_SLOT`, deriving `input_mt_init_slots()`-style slot-count intent from the staged ABS metadata without claiming input-core registration or transport-backed queue callbacks.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory teardown-observation helper that reports queue, status, config, and ABS staging state together with reset-local cleanup intent while preserving identity strings, without claiming remove, freeze, restore, or transport-backed teardown callbacks.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory registration-preflight summary that records when identity, capability, and multitouch slot-init intent are all present before any `input_register_device()` or transport-backed queue work.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory queue-callback preflight summary that records whether registration intent is staged, the event queue is filled, the status queue is configured, and the device is ready before any transport-backed callback or registration-lifecycle work.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory probe preflight summary that records whether identity, capability setup, registration intent, queue provisioning, and ready-state gating have all converged before any transport-backed probe handoff or input registration lifecycle work.

The live repo now includes one bounded driver-local registration blocker helper that keeps `input_register_device()` lifecycle, transport-backed queue callbacks, freeze or restore handling, and probe or remove work explicitly parked as `blocked_on_risky_transport` even after registration, queue-callback, and probe-preflight readiness all converge in memory.

Real event delivery, `input_register_device()` lifecycle coverage, freeze or restore behavior, and transport-backed queue callbacks remain too risky even with the landed queue-callback preflight helper, so the packet stays blocked below registration lifecycle work.
